skill.name: when-mapping-dependencies-use-dependency-mapper
skill.description: Maps project dependency trees, highlights package risks, and prepares dependency reports or visualizations across common package managers.
skill.summary: Analyze dependency structure, security signals, and package health for software projects.
skill.author: Claude Code

security_audit.summary: Most markdown and diagram detections are false positives caused by examples, fenced code blocks, or labels. Confirmed risks include npx Claude-Flow hooks, hidden cache reads, canned audit output, network token use, and unsanitized HTML tooltips. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace simulated counts and vulnerability messages with real package-manager analysis, or label the wrapper as a demo.
Require explicit user confirmation, pin package versions, and document data sent by pre-task, session-restore, post-task, and session-end hooks.

remediation.issue: Third-party vulnerability API and token use
remediation.suggestion: Make network scans opt in, avoid logging tokens, and document package data sent to Snyk or other services.
Build tooltip content with textContent or sanitized DOM nodes instead of assigning dependency metadata through innerHTML.
Use a user-approved cache path, define retention rules, and avoid copying hidden cache data into project outputs.

content.value_statement: Large dependency trees can hide security, version, and architecture risks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through dependency discovery, graph analysis, and reports.
actual_capabilities: Detects package manager patterns for npm, yarn, pnpm, pip, poetry, cargo, Maven, Go modules, bundler, composer, and NuGet.
Guides manifest and lock file review for direct and transitive dependency mapping.
Describes checks for circular dependencies, duplicate packages, outdated versions, and dependency depth.
Supports security review workflows using npm audit, Snyk, GitHub advisories, CVE sources, and OSV.
Defines console, JSON, HTML, SVG, GraphViz, and ASCII report formats.
Includes a slash-command wrapper that prepares agent instructions and Claude-Flow coordination hooks.
limitations: The shell wrapper prints simulated results unless an agent performs real analysis.
Network vulnerability checks can send package data to third-party services.
Snyk scanning needs a user-provided API token.
HTML visualization examples need sanitization before use with untrusted package metadata.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Audits
use_cases.description: Review direct and transitive packages before a release, with focus on vulnerabilities and outdated dependencies.

use_cases.title: Investigate Architecture Cycles
use_cases.description: Map dependency paths to find circular references, duplicate packages, and deep transitive chains.

use_cases.title: Create Supply Chain Reports
use_cases.description: Summarize package counts, security status, license checks, and remediation tasks for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Dependency Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dependency-mapper to analyze this project. Identify the package manager, direct dependencies, transitive dependency count, and the main risks.

prompt_templates.title: Security-Focused Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dependency-mapper with security analysis for this repository. Prioritize critical and high vulnerabilities, affected packages, and practical upgrade steps.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Dependency Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dependency-mapper to find circular dependencies, duplicate packages, deep dependency chains, and dependency groups that should be simplified.

prompt_templates.title: Full Supply Chain Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dependency-mapper to produce a full dependency risk report with vulnerability sources, license concerns, outdated packages, graph insights, and remediation.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Node.js project before release.
output: Detected npm with one manifest and one lock file.
Summarized direct and transitive dependency volume.
Prioritized vulnerable packages and recommended targeted updates.

output_examples.input: Review dependency architecture for a service with build conflicts.
output: Highlighted duplicate package versions that may cause runtime mismatch.
Flagged deep transitive chains for maintainer review.
Provided a dependency graph summary for the team.

output_examples.input: Prepare an executive dependency health summary.
output: Summarized dependency volume, security status, outdated packages, and license concerns.
Separated urgent fixes from long-term cleanup tasks.
Listed assumptions and external data sources used during review.

best_practices: Review the shell wrapper before running it on sensitive repositories.
Confirm network use before enabling third-party vulnerability checks.
Verify generated recommendations with the native package manager.
anti_patterns: Do not treat simulated console output as a completed audit.
Do not expose API tokens in shared logs or generated reports.
Do not publish generated HTML from untrusted metadata without sanitization.

faq.question: Which package managers does this skill describe?
faq.answer: It covers npm, yarn, pnpm, pip, poetry, pipenv, cargo, Maven, Gradle, Go modules, bundler, composer, and NuGet.

faq.question: Does it perform real vulnerability scanning by itself?
faq.answer: The documentation defines scanning workflows. The shell wrapper mainly prepares instructions and simulated output.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Network access is needed for current vulnerability data from services such as Snyk, GitHub advisories, CVE sources, or OSV.

faq.question: Can it generate visual dependency graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes HTML, SVG, GraphViz, and console visualizations for dependency trees and risk highlights.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Review the npx Claude-Flow commands, output directory, cache directory, and third-party API token use.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for sensitive projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. It is not blocked as malicious, but external command and network behaviors need approval.
